featured_reviews.review_text:

Personally, if I'm paying a bomb for an item, I expect good hygiene & at least some decent seating both are missing here.
In the early days, there were limited options available but the quality was up to the mark, now there's everything available but no food quality & taste. Putting an insane amount of cheese & cream doesn't make food tasty.
To sum up, try a sandwich, pani puri & dosa without a miss, they're still holding that old times charm.

featured_reviews.review_text:
One of the best pocket-friendly kulchas you’ll find in Mumbai. I’ve been here three times already and it never disappoints on the kulcha front.

The place is tucked away in a quiet corner, away from heavy traffic 🚶‍♂️, which makes the visit even better.

I tried the Aloo onion Cheese and Mix Veg Cheese kulchas — both were absolutely delicious 🤤, soft, and loaded with flavor. The only letdown was the chole. It felt watery, light on masala, and didn’t really match up to the kulchas 😕. But then again, for under ₹100 with unlimited chole, it’s hard to expect more.

Overall, I’d give this a solid ⭐⭐⭐⭐ - purely for the kulchas and value for the price. Totally worth it if you’re craving something tasty and budget-friendly 🙌.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavik Bhavnani
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re a fan of authentic, well-made kulchas, Sai Kripa does not disappoint. Their kulchas are:

✅ Perfectly Crisp & Fluffy – The outer layer has a satisfying crispiness, while the inside remains soft and slightly chewy.

✅ Well-Stuffed & Flavorful – Whether it’s aloo, paneer, or mixed stuffing, they don’t skimp on ingredients. The masala is balanced, with a slight tang and spice kick that complements the kulcha beautifully.

✅ Served with the Right Pairings – A good kulcha is incomplete without chole, raita, or chutney, and Sai Kripa gets this right. Their chole is rich and well-spiced, making for a fulfilling combination.

✅ Good Portion & Value for Money – Generous portions at reasonable pricing make it a great choice for a hearty meal.

Overall, if you’re looking for a place that nails a classic North Indian-style kulcha, Sai Kripa is worth a visit.

Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)

Worst Experience!

This was a corporate order, and we ended up waiting over an hour for our food, only to be met with complete disappointment.

Our order was significantly delayed, and despite calling the restaurant multiple times, no one answered. When I contacted the first delivery partner assigned to the order, he informed me that he had returned the parcel to the restaurant because the raita was leaking. What was frustrating was that neither the restaurant nor the delivery partner informed me about this. He then mentioned that another delivery partner would be assigned since he had already waited too long.

When the food finally arrived, we discovered that one of the main items, Kadhai Paneer, was missing. On top of that, none of the raitas or salads that were supposed to accompany the three biryanis were included.

This was a corporate meal, and several people were left hungry due to the missing items and poor handling of the order. As a Swiggy One member who orders regularly, this has been one of the worst experiences I've had. I will never order from Street Foods by Punjab Grill again and would strongly discourage others from doing so.

Very disappointing service and a complete lack of accountability.

featured_reviews.name: Eat In Ontario Blog
featured_reviews.review_text:
Time for a little backstory - despite coming to Mumbai every year all through my childhood, l'd never actually eaten in the Khau Galli due to the paranoia around falling ill easily. This time around though, I braved through the paranoia to indulge my inner foodie. And I am so glad I did because it led me to delicious fusion food at Cheese on Fire (Outside, Kesharwala Garden, 101, Khau Galli, Sindhu Wadi, Ghatkopar East, Mumbai, Maharashtra 400077). With a fiery grill and expert hands, this stall is renowned for its variety of momo, pizza, and pasta dishes.
We started off the meal with an order of 6 pizza shots to warm up for the meal ahead! A tiny pani puri stuffed with pizza sauce, cheese, and a drop of hot sauce, the dish didn't have too much of the 'pizza' aspect but was delicious nonetheless. With just the right amount of cheese, the tiny puri was filling without being too cloying while the pizza sauce and hot sauce added a tangy and spicy kick to the dish. On the whole, it was a great segue into the Paneer Tandoori Momos.
Watching the Paneer Tandoori Momos being grilled was an experience on its own with the staff quickly flipping the stuffed momos on the tandoor to give its signature smoky flavour. The essence of the momos lay in its crust this time around - the charred flavours of the grill brought out the comforting paneer flavours within, made only better with the variety of chutneys and eggless mayonnaise (highly recommended if you have not tried it already) on the side.
In conquering the Khau Galli apprehensions of my childhood, I stumbled upon the culinary gem, Cheese on Fire, and it was a revelation of flavors and fear-defying indulgence. Should you find yourself in Ghatkopar suddenly craving either momos or pizza, l would highly recommend checking them out!

To hear more about this review, follow us @eatinontario on Instagram, TikTok, & Facebook. ✨🤩🙏

featured_reviews.name: Rajesh Gohil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Very disappointing experience at the Radhe Ghatkopar branch.

I had pre-booked 2.5 kg (₹1113) of biryani at 11:00 AM and clearly informed the staff that I needed it by 5:00 PM. When I arrived at 5:00 PM, the staff seemed unaware of the order and started asking who had taken it. After checking with others, they informed me that the biryani is not ready and would take another 30–40 minutes to prepare. If customers have to wait that long despite pre-booking and making full payment in advance, it defeats the purpose of placing an advance order.

The most concerning part was the food quality. Around 1 kg of biryani was left over, so we stored it in the refrigerator overnight. By the next morning, it had spoiled. In comparison, homemade dhokla prepared on the same day and stored under the same conditions remained perfectly fine. This raises concerns about the ingredients, spices, and overall quality standards being maintained.

My observations:
• Excessive waiting time, even for pre-booked orders.
• Food taste and quality is questionable.
• Minimum order quantity is 250 (it's fixed) grams per plate. They never give food in custom quantities as required.
. The cooks are Nepali, and we were expecting a traditional Gujarati taste, unfortunately the taste did not meet our expectations.

Overall, the experience was disappointing and needs significant improvement in both service and quality and taste control.

I give it a negative -5 out of 5 stars.

featured_reviews.name: The Tailor Eats
featured_reviews.review_text:
When you put heart into the food you prepare even the simplest of ingredients seems like magic potions. Here is one such man who has been spreading love since 1984 from a roadside curb of Aarey. Situated in the silent bylanes of Ghatkopar this place was easy to find thanks to Google maps.

When I walked in my first instinct was to ask for a menu and he very smirkingly said beta pichle 30 saal se menu nahi banaya hai sab ko pata hai uncle k idar kya milta hai. It was 6pm and I was hungry for my evening filling but then I was kinda met with a little disappointment. When I reached his samosas were over ! 😅
An eatery joint in Mumbai affords to say we are done for the day at 6pm 😰

But when the conversations went deeper is when I understood this man has found his optimal living. He starts off at 9am and by 6pm his items are sold out! And he does this all alone. Keeping health as first priority he does this with utmost passion which keeps bringing his loyalists again and again.

In the absence of Samosas he whipped out a Lays Pav for me. This has been a never ever tried combination for me but then I was blown away. I first believed it was delicious because I was hungry😆 but then when I started deciphering the taste layers the magic was in the 3 chutneys which he makes by himself with a tinge of love sprinkled on top of every food item which was served across the counter. The genuinity of the person oozed in his words and I believe transformed in his food.

The fun fact remains though he is known for his samosas but they are sourced from the very famous Gurukripa. But then still upwards of 400+ people come to his stall to have the samosa he feeds. The magic potion is the chutney guys! 🤫

Will definitely recommend everyone to go feast on some delicious food and meet this vibrant man. But whatever that is the thumb rule being 6 baje se pehle jao! 😌

Cheers!

featured_reviews.name: Sankalp P
featured_reviews.review_text:
The No. 13 Pink Sauce Pasta on the menu is an absolute game-changer. It combines a rich, creamy pink sauce with an irresistible blend of perfectly sautéed veggies, creating a taste that transports you straight to a high-end café or restaurant. Each bite bursts with a harmonious balance of flavors—rich yet light, with a velvety texture that coats the pasta just right. The vegetables add a fresh, vibrant crunch, elevating the dish to another level. We couldn't help but dive in, and the foodgasm was so intense, it felt like the perfect bite we never wanted to end.
Simply divine!

featured_reviews.name: Pallavi Jain
featured_reviews.review_text: I recently tried the food at WTC Past, a street food shop in Mumbai, and it was absolutely mind-blowing! The flavors were incredible, and everything was made to perfection. If you're a fan of Jain cuisine, or even if you're just looking to try something unique, this place is a must-try.

featured_reviews.name: Siddhanth Vaishya
featured_reviews.review_text:
Overview & Recommendation:

Located in Khau Gali of Ghatkopar, this is a classic joint which has to offer a variety of Pasta. It’s into the limelight for their delish Pink Sauce Pasta. It has a stall near Gurukripa Hotel and also one in the main Khau Gali. If you want to put your money where your mouth is, go for the Pink Sauce pasta with a leap of faith.

F&B:

1) Pink Sauce Pasta - Penne (also known as Red and White sauce pasta) (4.5 on scale of 5)

This is a treat to your taste buds. Anytime if you feel you want to celebrate a cheat day then reward yourself with a pink sauce Pasta (combination of Red sauce, White Sauce, Amul cream, Cheese and other infinity sauces) which has outburst of Italian flavours in a desi style. It has Corn, Onions, Capsicums infused in the pink sauce which is so perfectly balanced. Its a bit heavy to eat, but so worth it.

VFM (4 on scale of 5):

It costs nearly 300 bucks which I would say is on a higher side for a street joint which has no ambience or seating to offer. But definitely its flavory and delicious which trumps the cost part.
